sri-lanka.title: Flag of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

colors.note: Represents the Sinhalese majority and the gold lion of the ancient Kingdom of Kandy
Border representing the Buddhist teaching of the middle path and unifying all communities
Vertical stripe representing the Muslim minority
Vertical stripe representing the Tamil minority

desc:
- Two vertical stripes of green and orange at the hoist, beside a maroon panel bearing a gold lion holding a sword, all within a yellow border and with a bo leaf in each corner of the maroon panel
- Originally adopted in 1951 and modified in 1972 with four bo leaves replacing spearheads

countryData.name: Sri Lanka
countryData.officialName: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
countryData.location: island in the Indian Ocean, South Asia

trivia:
- Also known as the Lion Flag, the design is based on the royal standard of the last king of Kandy, seized by the British in 1815
- The bo leaves represent the four Buddhist virtues of kindness, compassion, equanimity, and happiness
- The flag is among the oldest continuous national symbols still in use, with the lion motif dating back more than two millennia
